definition: The side of the body that is opposite the right side.
example: Turn left at the end of the road.
note: Italian capital letter removed, and the definition simplified so it pairs naturally with 'right'.

definition: The side of the body that is opposite the left side.
example: Turn right at the traffic lights.
note: Had been changed to mean 'morally good'. The list already teaches 'left' as a direction, and the original German and Italian were both the direction, so this now completes the pair. The 'correct' meaning is already covered by the word 'correct'.

definition: To sit on and control a bike, horse, or animal as it moves.
example: We can ride our bikes to the park.
note: Italian capital letter removed.

definition: A place where goods are sold.
example: I need to go to the shop to buy some milk.
note: French 'boutique' means a small fashion shop. The everyday word for going to the shop is 'magasin'.

definition: To begin doing something.
example: Let's start our English lesson now and learn new words.
note: German 'starten' is used for engines and races. For starting a lesson the natural word is 'anfangen'.

definition: Feeling certain that something is true.
example: I am sure about the answer to the question.
note: Italian capital letter removed.

definition: A piece of writing; written words.
example: The teacher asked us to read the text on page ten.
note: All four translations mean 'a piece of writing', but the example was about a phone message. Example rewritten so it matches.

definition: Toward a higher place or position.
example: The balloon floated up into the blue sky.
note: The example was two unrelated sentences and the second one ('Time is up') used a completely different meaning. Replaced with one clear sentence.

definition: A person who comes to see a place or another person.
example: The visitor enjoyed the beautiful exhibits at the museum.
note: The example said 'museum' twice. Cleaned up.

definition: A method of doing something.
example: This is a good way to learn new vocabulary.
note: German 'Weg' means a path or road, not a method, so it did not match the other three. Changed to 'Art'.

definition: Used to talk about something that happens in the future.
example: She will visit her grandma next week.
note: Italian said 'volere', which means 'to want' and is simply wrong here. Italian has no separate word for 'will', so the entry now shows that it is made with a future ending. French brackets removed.

definition: Used to say politely what you want, or to talk about something imagined.
example: I would like a cup of tea, please.
note: Had been built around a rare use ('as a child I would visit the park'). The first thing a learner meets is 'I would like'. German was the only translation that matched that, and now all four do.

definition: Used to introduce a fact that makes the main idea surprising.
example: Although it was raining, we still went for a walk.
note: Italian capital letter removed.

definition: To come into sight; to become possible to see.
example: A rainbow appeared in the sky after the rain.
note: Had been changed to the weaker meaning 'to seem'. All three original translations were 'to come into view', which is the first meaning of 'appear'. Restored, with a matching example.

definition: To make a formal request, for example for a job.
example: She will apply for a new job next month.
note: Spanish 'postular' is mainly Latin American; 'solicitar' is understood everywhere. Italian shortened to the natural phrase.

definition: The result of adding numbers together and dividing by how many there are.
example: The average of four and six is five.
note: All four translations had been changed from the thing to a describing word, based on an awkward example ('the average student'). Every original translation was the thing, which is the first meaning. Fully restored.

definition: A place where people go to buy and drink drinks.
example: We met our friends at the bar for a drink.
note: Had been changed to 'a long piece of metal'. Three of the four original translations were the drinking place, which is what anyone thinks of first. Restored.

definition: A place where people go to buy and drink drinks.
example: We met our friends at the bar for a drink.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: A large, strong wild animal with thick fur.
example: A large brown bear walked slowly through the forest.
note: Had been changed to the rare verb 'to bear a heavy load'. The first meaning of 'bear' is the animal, which is what the original French showed. Rebuilt around the animal.

definition: A large, strong wild animal with thick fur.
example: A large brown bear walked slowly through the forest.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: The lowest part of something.
example: The ship sank to the bottom of the ocean.
note: Italian had an unnecessary 'the' in front of it.

definition: To feel that someone or something is important to you.
example: She cares deeply about her students' progress.
note: The example was broken ('her students's students' progress'). All four translations were different shapes; they now match each other.

definition: An event where people try to win by being the best.
example: The athletic competition was very exciting for everyone involved.
note: The example ended with stray words ('for everyone involved teams'). Cleaned up.

definition: To make something the same as another thing.
example: Please copy the text into your notebook.
note: Spanish capital letter removed.

definition: Going straight from one place to another without stopping.
example: We took a direct flight to Rome with no stops.
note: Had been changed to a rare use ('can you direct me to the bus stop'). The first meaning of 'direct' is 'straight, without stops', which is what the original German showed. All four now match.

definition: Twice as much or twice as many.
example: He ordered a double portion of ice cream.
note: Had been turned into the action 'to double a recipe'. The first meaning of 'double' is 'twice as much', which is what the original German and French showed. Restored.

definition: The activity of controlling and steering a vehicle.
example: She enjoys driving her car to new places on holiday.
note: French was the noun for driving while the others were the activity, so they did not match. Now all four express the same idea.

definition: To let something fall by accident.
example: Please be careful, do not drop the plate.
note: Italian spelling corrected ('fare cadere' becomes 'far cadere'). Example tidied.

definition: Without any water or liquid; not wet.
example: The towel is dry now, so you can use it.
note: Had been turned into the action 'to dry something'. The first meaning of 'dry' is the opposite of wet, which is what the original German and French showed. Restored.

definition: To come or go into a place.
example: Please enter the room quietly.
note: Spanish 'ingresar' is formal and used for hospitals and bank deposits. The everyday word is 'entrar'.

definition: Having too much flesh on the body; not thin.
example: The cat is very fat because it eats too much.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: A shape, especially the shape of a person.
example: She drew a simple figure of a person on the paper.
note: The entry had been built around 'figure out', which is a two-word phrase, not the word 'figure' itself. Rebuilt around the real word, matching the original Spanish.

definition: An animal that lives in water and breathes through gills.
example: The fish swam quickly in the clear blue water.
note: Spanish has two words: 'pez' is the living animal and 'pescado' is fish as food. The definition described the animal but the example and Spanish word were about food. Everything now describes the animal.

definition: To be the right size or shape for someone.
example: These shoes fit me perfectly; they are very comfortable.
note: Spanish 'entrar' means to go in. For clothes fitting, the natural phrase is 'quedar bien'. French shortened to one clear option.

definition: A set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a building.
example: They live in a small flat on the third floor.
note: 'Flat' appears twice in the list with two different Spanish words. Both now use 'apartamento', which is understood everywhere.

definition: To give all your attention to one thing.
example: Please focus on your homework and not the TV.
note: German 'fokussieren' is technical and mostly used for cameras. Changed to the everyday word. Italian trailing word removed so all four match.

definition: An empty space between two things.
example: There is a gap between the two fence posts.
note: Spanish 'brecha' means a breach or a wide divide. For a physical space between two objects the word is 'hueco'.

definition: The place where you live.
example: I am going home after work today.
note: German was written in lower case as an old-fashioned word. The normal German word for home is 'Zuhause'.
